newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-CENTRAL BANK DEFENDS NEW BANK REQUIREMENTS.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-CENTRAL BANK DEFENDS NEW BANK REQUIREMENTS.

text.p: The Estonian central bank said on Thursday that it does not believe that the economy is over heating but increased capital adequacy requirements as some risk factors had emerged.

The central bank yesterday announced it was increasing capital adequacy requirements for banks from eight percent to 10 percent amid worries over the rapid growth in credit and fears by some economists that the economy was over-heating.

"The central Bank does not believe that the economy is out of balance but with the rapid growth in banking and on the stock market some risk factors have emerged", Aare Jarvan, head of the bank's policy department, told Reuters.
"The decision is to be considered as a cautionary measure taken in conditions of tough competition to help the banks to follow a more conservative loan policy," he added.
The decision was taken with the full knowledge of the government and the commericial banks.
"The central bank is in constant consulation with the banks and has expressed its concern on the growth of risks," he said.
"The previous and present governments have been aware of these steps and has supported them," he added.
As for Estonia's plans to take a country credit rating, the central bank sees the new capital adequacy requirments as one way of reducing risks after a postive rating, Jarvan added.
